findings.claim: The requireManageMembers() Javadoc references canManage() when it should reference canManageMembership(GroupModel).
The requireManageMembers Javadoc says it throws when canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false, but the implementation checks canManageMembers.

RealmAdminPermissionsConfig adds AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS to the shared test fixture. This can hide regressions in the Groups resource-type permission path for tests that should not satisfy the group list gate.

GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission() and adds it to the result. That is the authorization resource ID, not the group ID (groupResource.getName()). hasPermission() resolves by name, so the per-group lookup fails, and the returned IDs do not match group IDs used in user filtering and counts.

Per-group resources are created without a type, because getOrCreateResource() never calls setType. As a result, findByType(server, 'Groups', ...) returns only the all-groups type resource and not the per-group resources.

With only per-group VIEW_MEMBERS permission in V2, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns an empty set. users().count()/getUsersCount then returns 0 while /users returns members through the post-filter. Pagination is applied before the canView post-filter, which produces short pages.
The getGroupIdsWithViewPermission Javadoc says '@return Stream of IDs', but the method returns Set<String>.
The getGroupIdsWithViewPermission Javadoc does not mention that V2 returns the type-resource ID instead of actual group IDs.

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg) falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). An admin with only all-groups VIEW permission therefore passes requireManage(). This lets them create top-level groups and move groups to top level in GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup, which is guarded only by requireManage().
The canManage() Javadoc states that V2 VIEW permission is enough to manage groups.

The canViewGlobal short-circuit was removed from group listing in GroupsResource and GroupResource getSubGroups, so every listing goes through canView(g), which lacks the realm-wide canView() check. Admins with global Groups VIEW/MANAGE but no per-group grants get empty listings.
The V1 feature check was moved from event time to listener registration time. Runs that enable V1 at runtime with skipRestart=true never register the role/client/group-removed cleanup listener.

The AdminPermissions cleanup listener for role/client/group removal is registered only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. In V2-only deployments, removed roles, clients and groups leave orphaned authorization resources and permissions.
response.getLocation() can be null even with a 201 status, which causes an NPE when parsing the path.
UserPermissionsV2 dropped the AdminRoles.ADMIN fast-path. Users with only the umbrella admin role fail the canView/canManage/canMapRoles/canManageGroupMembership checks.
The switch(resourceType) throws NullPointerException for a null resource type, where the previous if-chain threw IllegalStateException.
The new Groups resource type and its scopes (manage-membership, manage-members, view-members) have no documentation.
getResourceName is not extended for GROUPS. Group permission resources show a null display name, and the type resource has no 'All groups' label.
The new test file has a copyright year of 2024.

In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, getResourceTypeResource can return null, and the result is passed directly to policyStore.findByResource(server, null). This causes an NPE (HTTP 500) on group checks.
There is a stray ';;' at line 68 of the new test file.
No migration adds the Groups type resource and the new scopes to realms whose admin-permissions client already exists, because init() returns early in that case.
hasPermission evaluates either the per-group resource or the all-groups type resource, never both. Once a per-group permission exists for a group, all-groups grants no longer apply to it.
GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission lacks the resourceId filter that UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission uses to prevent permission leakage across resources.
GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission is a third near-copy of the V2 evaluator in UserPermissionsV2 and ClientPermissionsV2, and the copies have already diverged.
The test wraps the call in try(Response) and assertEquals(CREATED) before ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse. This is redundant, since handleCreatedResponse already asserts 201 and closes the response.

When a group has no per-group resource, evaluating the all-groups type resource pulls in every per-group permission. A VIEW permission on one group therefore grants VIEW on every group that lacks its own resource.
The @BeforeEach comment contains the typo 'initializaed'.
The canView() Javadoc says 'Or if it has a permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups' without the 'For V2 only' qualifier, but V1 canView() checks roles only.
There are no tests for all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS, users().count(), VIEW-only write attempts, or mixed all-groups and per-group permissions.
canMapRole() checks root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS) and then calls checkAdminRoles(role) instead of returning true, which removes the users-manage shortcut.
